definitions.explanation: The final day of any month. Originally meant the thirtieth day, but now refers to the last day regardless of how many days the month has.

examples.japanese: {三十日|みそか}に{支払|しはら}いをする。
examples.english: I make payments on the last day of the month.

examples.japanese: {毎月|まいつき}の{三十日|みそか}に{締|し}め{切|き}りがある。
examples.english: There is a deadline on the last day of every month.

examples.japanese: {二月|にがつ}の{三十日|みそか}は{二十八日|にじゅうはちにち}か{二十九日|にじゅうくにち}になる。
examples.english: The last day of February falls on the 28th or 29th.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {三十日|みそか} literally means the thirtieth day ({三十|みそ} is an old counting word for thirty + {日|か}, day). It has come to mean the last day of any month.

RELATED WORDS:
- {大晦日|おおみそか}: New Year's Eve (literally 'great last day') — the last day of the year, December 31st
- {晦日|みそか}: an alternate kanji spelling with the same meaning

USAGE: Less common in everyday speech than {月末|げつまつ} (end of the month), but {三十日|みそか} has a traditional feel and is still used, especially in set phrases and financial contexts. The derived word {大晦日|おおみそか} is extremely common.
